thread:
elena: Customer (acct org_9f3) reporting intermittent 429s during bursts. They say org quota shows plenty of headroom but a single API key is getting blocked. Traffic goes through a partner proxy that rewrites egress IP. Can someone confirm how our rate-limiter decides scope when multiple signals (API key, X-Redwood-Org header, X-Forwarded-For) are present? They provided a minimal repro.

jon: @elena - can you grab the response headers (request-id, x-rw-rate-scope) and a raw request sample (mask the key) so we can see what attribution was returned?

elena: Pasting headers from their failing call: `x-rw-request-id: rq_8a7f`, `x-rw-rate-code: 429`, `x-rw-rate-scope: api_key`, `x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0`. Their curl (via partner) looked like: `curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-xxxxx' -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 10.1.2.3' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — note proxy egress IP is 52.18.9.7 (so remote_addr is proxy). They sometimes included `X-Redwood-Org: org_9f3` but partner drops unknown headers.

samir: quick note on behavior: attribution order is basically API key -> project binding -> explicit org header -> IP-derived bucket. However there are a couple of edgecases: (a) if the API key is bound to a project with its own quota and that project is exhausted, you'll see api_key-scoped 429 even if org still has capacity; (b) if the API key lookup fails (expired or unrecognized) we fall back to org or IP; (c) proxy-config differences can cause us to see the proxy addr not the original client, which can push traffic into a shared NAT bucket.

elena: ok so the key could legitimately be the problem even if org ok. customer insists the same key used elsewhere doesn't hit limit though.

samir: two more possibilities: 1) eventual consistency / counter replication: quota counters are replicated and under a burst you can hit a pod that thinks the key is at limit (rare but possible); 2) there was a recent change to how we trust `X-Forwarded-For` and we only honor it when `x-rw-proxy-trust: true` is present from partner — if that's missing we attribute to the proxy IP.

jon: +1. Also check if partner is NATting multiple customers behind same egress addr. Shared NAT + conservative per-IP bucket explains surprising 429s when org-level looks fine. Can you ask for `x-rw-auth-attrib` in the debug headers? We can flip a flag to include attribution in responses for support repros.

elena: repro steps I provided the customer:
1) call API directly (bypass proxy) with same key and compare 429s
2) call with a different API key from same client to see per-key vs per-ip behavior
3) add `X-Redwood-Org: org_9f3` in request to test org-header fallback

Example curl to bypass proxy:

```bash
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-xxxxx' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
```

ops: looked up rq_8a7f - we see ~120 requests from 52.18.9.7 in 30s. The API key bucket shows drops/overflow and the response included `x-rw-rate-scope: api_key`. I temporarily enabled attribution debug for that org; new responses will include `x-rw-auth-attrib: api_key(project:proj-77)`.

elena: Customer ran the direct call and 429s stopped. They updated partner to forward `X-Redwood-Org` and enabled sticky egress on their side; issue went away. They were happy. Recommendation: add KB note recommending partners forward explicit org header and enable sticky NAT or per-client egress where possible.

samir: I'll add a short KB and open a telemetry ticket to ensure `auth.attribution` is emitted on all 429 responses going forward, and a follow-up PR to surface `quota_bucket` in debug response headers.

sre-bot: deploy 2026-03-16T11:22Z: feature/telemetry-auth-attrib -> prod rollout started :rocket:

elena: thanks all, closing loop with customer and adding steps to the support template.
